details:
Ghost Fleet X: where satellites and ships stop agreeing.

Ships are meant to broadcast their identity and position over AIS, but a transmitter can be switched off, and a vessel that goes quiet is hard to track. Radar satellites see ships whether or not they transmit. The gap between what radar detects and what AIS reports is therefore worth investigating, and Ghost Fleet X turns that gap into a change-monitoring tool for the global ocean.

The ocean is divided into 3,315 cells about 150 km across. For each cell and each month since 2020, the app counts unmatched Sentinel-1 radar detections per satellite pass, giving the Maritime Signal Drift Index. Each series is then corrected one step at a time for satellite coverage, AIS reception, season, and wind (NASA POWER data). The corrected trends are tested with a Mann-Kendall test adjusted for autocorrelation, Sen’s slope for the size of the change, and Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery control. Neighbouring cells that agree are merged into a single event. Each event is then rerun under seven alternative analyses, and the app reports which ones it survives. The published scan finds 230 lasting changes: 173 falling and 57 rising.

The map also shows context from other public sources: ships that switched AIS off (808 in the 30 days shown on the live site on 15 November 2026), groups that went dark together, meetings at sea, possible fishing inside protected areas, possible oil slicks from SkyTruth’s Cerulean model with candidate ships, offshore platforms, and two NASA imagery layers, night lights and ocean chlorophyll.

Every result is shown with its limits. A cause panel ranks how much of each change the ordinary explanations absorb. Confidence is capped at Moderate, because one radar sensor is not enough for High. Each event exports as a case file with the evidence, the alternatives, the limits, and a suggested next step. Every statement is labelled observation, inference, hypothesis, or recommendation. Unmatched never means illegal: a gap can come from a missing transmitter, a reception problem, or a matching failure. Ghost Fleet X gives investigators leads, never accusations.

The app has a Python back end with NumPy statistics served by FastAPI, and a React front end drawn with MapLibre. It uses free public data only.
